entry.title: Request for position: Layout Instability API CSS pixel attribution
entry.content:
Information about the proposal

  • Explainer URL: WICG/layout-instability#125
  • Specification URL: https://wicg.github.io/layout-instability/
  • TAG Review: Not applicable (compatibility fix for existing API)
  • Chromium bug: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/399058544
  • ChromeStatus: https://chromestatus.com/feature/5155103518228480

Summary

The Layout Instability API currently reports attribution rectangles (prevRect and currentRect) in device pixels. This proposal changes them to CSS pixels for consistency with other Web Platform APIs (e.g., getBoundingClientRect, IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver).

Key changes:

  • prevRect and currentRect now use CSS pixels instead of device pixels
  • Aligns with standard coordinate space used across the web platform
  • Improves consistency for developers measuring layout stability
  • Minimal breaking change (primarily affects telemetry/monitoring tools)

Motivation:

Device pixels create inconsistencies across different device pixel ratios and make it harder for developers to correlate layout shift data with other measurements. CSS pixels are the standard coordinate system for web content.

Compatibility:

This is behind a flag in Chrome. We're seeking feedback from other vendors before enabling by default.

We'd appreciate Mozilla's position on this compatibility improvement.

entry.title: WebUSB rejection + summary statement is written by someone who doesn't understand website browser permissions are per-site (nor that users can safely have informed consent) - Please seek external evaluation
entry.content:
Web-USB API:

🔗 WebUSB API negative Proposal #100 MDN 📊

Description

This document describes an API for securely providing access to Universal Serial Bus devices from web pages.

Rationale

Because many USB devices are not designed to handle potentially-malicious interactions over the USB protocols and because those devices can have significant effects on the computer they're connected to, we believe that the security risks of exposing USB devices to the Web are too broad to risk exposing users to them or to explain properly to end users to obtain meaningful informed consent. It also poses risks that sites could use USB device identity or data stored on USB devices as tracking identifiers.

Counter argument:

This is not factually correct if browsers respect users privacy and do not allow fingerprinting of USB devices without the site having permission for web-usb (per site permission like webcam/mic/file-api).

It also carries the same risk as the serial api, file api, and many users would compare the webcam/microphone api's as of similar or greater risk. It's about informing the user, deny by default (always deny without user agreement + first ui interaction triggering connect), and per site permissions.

The equivalent utility to web-usb which is actually used in most educational / microcontroller development is the Serial API or web-serial, which has generally worse support (caniuse.com), yet is effectively similar in danger/merit, but scores a "Neutral" position from Mozilla (you don't like it but don't reject it).
It amuses me to know that android can get around some serial api issues by using the web-usb polyfill, even including new serial drivers if needed (bundled into the webkit app). The wonders of technology never cease (when not gate-kept)...

Web Serial API:

🔗 Serial API neutral Proposal #336 bug 📊

Description

The Serial API provides a way for websites to read and write from a serial device through script. Such an API would bridge the web and the physical world, by allowing documents to communicate with devices such as microcontrollers, 3D printers, and other serial devices. There is also a companion explainer document.

Rationale

Devices that offer serial interfaces often expose powerful, low-level functions over the interface with little or no authentication. Exposing that sort of capability to the web without adequate safeguards presents a significant threat to those devices. A user deliberately installing a site-specific add-on may be adequate, given sufficiently understandable consent copy.

Please get a qualified group of people to actually review the situations, so the millions of educational users (makeCode w/microbit, micropython, Arduino compatible boards, Espressif's ESP32 families, edublocks) and hobbyists and professionals can finally use Firefox again. More than that though, people still hold Mozilla/MDN and their statements in high regard, so getting past this would be great.

entry.title: [SVG] Support width & height attributes on <use> and x, y, width & height on<symbol> elements as presentation attributes
entry.content:
Specification title

Support width & height attributes on and x, y, width & height on elements as presentation attributes

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/styling.html#TermPresentationAttribute

Explainer URL (if available)

No response

Proposal author(s)

No response

MDN URL

No response

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

No response

Mozillians who can provide input

No response

WebKit standards-position

No response

Other information

This feature enables consistent rendering of the element when specifying width and height via both CSS and presentation attributes. It also adds support for x, y, width, and height as presentation attributes on , giving developers greater control over SVG layout and positioning.

With this feature, the following two HTML examples will now produce the same output:

Using CSS for [1]:

<svg width="100px" height="100px">
 <defs>
    <symbol id="sym">
      <rect width="100px" height="100px" fill="green"/>
    </symbol>
  </defs>
  <use href="#sym" style="width:40px; height:40px"/>
</svg>

Using Presentation Attributes for [2]:

<svg width="100px" height="100px">
 <defs>
    <symbol id="sym" width="80px" height="80px" x="10" y="10">
      <rect width="100px" height="100px" fill="green"/>
    </symbol>
  </defs>
  <use href="#sym" width="40px" height="40px"/>
</svg>

In Firefox, example [2] does not currently render correctly—width and height set via presentation attributes on are not applied as expected.

entry.title: TCP Socket Pool Limit Randomization
entry.content:
Specification title

TCP Socket Pool Limit Randomization

Proposal author(s)

@arichiv

Bugzilla URL

https://crbug.com/415691664

TAG Review

w3ctag/design-reviews#1151

WebKit standards-position

WebKit/standards-positions#550

Chrome standards position

https://chromestatus.com/feature/6496757559197696

Other information

By exploiting limits in the connection pool size on Chrome, knowledge can be gained about cross-site state which would otherwise be inaccessible. Specifically, it’s possible (with some statistical certainty) to evaluate the login state, visited history, or even something more specific like whether gmail has pending messages in the inbox.

To mitigate this we are adding randomization to the way that TCP socket pools are limited so that an observing site cannot infer this information with high certainty.
